original_question: In the same layered construction G_n(phi), is it true that for sufficiently small nonzero phi the finite sequence of suspension angles phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) never repeats a value? Equivalently, does this force G_n(phi) to be a geodesic net in which all edges have weight one, while still having 14 unbalanced vertices and, for large n, arbitrarily many balanced vertices?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.5.8 in §4.5.1 of Section 4 ("The Star"), read together with Definitions 4.5.1–4.5.2, Fact 4.5.4, Lemma 4.5.5, Fact 4.5.6, and the preceding derivative-based Conjecture 4.5.7.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the same layered construction G_n(φ), the small nonzero deviation parameter φ, the finite sequence of suspension angles φ_0(φ), …, φ_n(φ), the non-repetition condition, and the intended consequence that the construction should give a geodesic net with all edge weights equal to 1, while retaining 14 unbalanced vertices and allowing arbitrarily many balanced vertices for large n.
missing_details: The paper formulates this as a conjecture, not as a proved statement.
The official target is specifically the small-nonzero-φ statement of Conjecture 4.5.8, not just an informal question about overlap.
The suspension angles φ_i(φ) must be defined as in Definitions 4.5.1 and 4.5.2: odd layers use one-hook suspension angles, even layers use two-hook suspension angles.
The finite sequence is finite because G_n(φ) has finitely many layers V_0, …, V_n; that layer notation is part of the nearby context.

The paper works with φ in a small allowed interval around 0 coming from the smooth-dependence and feasibility analysis; your draft says 'sufficiently small' but does not mention that this interval is inherited from the construction.

The implication to 'all edges have weight one' is justified in the paper via Lemma 4.5.5; the paper does not explicitly prove the converse, so your word 'Equivalently' is stronger than what is stated.

The nearby paper-faithful context includes Fact 4.5.6, namely φ_i(0)=0 for all i, and Conjecture 4.5.7, namely that the derivative sequence φ_i'(0) never repeats; Conjecture 4.5.8 is presented as following from those two ingredients.
The construction is initially a geodesic multinet; the point of the conjecture is that after small nonzero deviation it should actually be a geodesic net.
The paper states the 14 unbalanced vertices are of arbitrary degree; your draft omits that qualifier.

A nearby nuance in Lemma 4.5.5 is that it would actually be enough for the suspension angles to be distinct within the same parity class, since even and odd layers never have suspension edges in common.
refined_question: In the star construction of Section 4, let G_n(φ) be the layered deviated multinet with layers V_0, …, V_n obtained from a deviation parameter φ in the small allowed interval around 0, and let φ_i(φ) denote the suspension angle of layer V_i as defined in Definitions 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 (so odd i use one-hook suspensions, even i use two-hook suspensions, φ_0(φ)=φ, and φ_i(0)=0 for all i). Is it true that, for a fixed n and all sufficiently small nonzero φ, the finite sequence φ_0(φ), φ_1(φ), …, φ_n(φ) has no repeated value? If so, then by Lemma 4.5.5 the resulting G_n(φ) is in fact a geodesic net, not merely a geodesic multinet, with all edges of weight 1; together with the properties established earlier in the construction, this would produce examples with 14 unbalanced vertices of arbitrary degree and, as n grows, arbitrarily many balanced vertices.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Conjecture 4.5.8, not the earlier derivative conjecture 4.5.7. The wording 'for sufficiently small nonzero φ the finite sequence of suspension angles never repeats' matches Conjecture 4.5.8 almost directly. The surrounding context needed to make that stand-alone is supplied immediately nearby: Definitions 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 define the suspension angles, Fact 4.5.4 notes the sequence is finite because there are finitely many layers, Lemma 4.5.5 gives the implication to weight-one edges, Fact 4.5.6 and Conjecture 4.5.7 explain why the authors expect the small-nonzero-φ statement, and §4.1 together with §4.3.1 states the intended payoff of 14 unbalanced vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices. The only substantive correction to your draft is that the paper states an implication, not an explicit equivalence.
